pages.text: The wireless Chishi Energy network treats the $(bold)identity card as a key$(): every card carries a unique ID, and once authorized by a terminal it can be used to bind remote ports for cross-chunk and even $(bold)cross-dimension$() energy transfer — no pipes required.$(br2)A network consists of three parts:$(li)A terminal multiblock (transfer hub)$(li)Identity cards (authentication keys)$(li)Input/Output ports (remote transceivers)

$(bold)Core flow:$(br)1. Build the terminal multiblock; once formed, the network registers$(br)2. Authorize identity cards on the terminal's Security page (up to 8)$(br)3. Hold an authorized card and right-click an input/output port to bind$(br)4. The port looks up the terminal by card every tick; once authenticated, transfer starts$(br2)$(bold)Key traits:$() Revoking a card's authorization disconnects its ports remotely; ports do not need to sit on the terminal wall — place them anywhere; cross-dimension transfer requires a Dim Bridge component inside the structure.
